title: True sharing, false sharing and per-thread state under explicit placement
question: When two placed threads increment relaxed atomic counters, how does the measured thread's steady-state cost per increment depend on whether the counters share one slot, share one 64-byte line, or live 128 bytes apart, and does the answer change when the threads share a core (SMT siblings) instead of only the L3?
design_target: AMD Ryzen 3 7330U (family 19h, model 50h, Zen 3), Linux 7.0.0-42, perf 7.0.14. CPU numbers and the line size are this host's; on another host edit the variants and placements and re-check the events.

placements.name: cross-core
placements.meaning: measured thread on CPU 2, peer on CPU 4: different cores (private L1D and L2 each), one shared L3

placements.name: smt-siblings
placements.meaning: measured thread on CPU 2, peer on CPU 3: two hardware threads of one core sharing its L1D and L2

ex_ret_instr.justification: perf list (amdzen3): Retired Instructions. The kernel maps the generic PERF_COUNT_HW_INSTRUCTIONS to 0x00c0 on family 19h (amd_zen2_perfmon_event_map, selected by amd_pmu_event_map for x86 >= 0x19, arch/x86/events/amd/core.c, Linux v7.0) and sysfs events/instructions reads event=0xc0. Every layout runs the same loop, so equal instructions per increment confirm that only addresses changed.

ls_not_halted_cyc.justification: perf list: Cycles not in Halt; the kernel's generic PERF_COUNT_HW_CPU_CYCLES on family 19h (0x0076; sysfs events/cpu-cycles = event=0x76). User-mode cycles of the counting thread only (exclude_kernel). Cycles divided by elapsed nanoseconds gives an effective user-cycle rate, a check for frequency differences.

ls_dmnd_fills_from_sys.int_cache.justification: perf list: Demand Data Cache Fills by Data Source, From L3 or different L2 in same CCX. A fill of this core's L1D from another core's L2 or the shared L3 is what a line moving between private caches looks like from the requesting core.

ls_dmnd_fills_from_sys.lcl_l2.role: control: fills from the core's own L2
ls_dmnd_fills_from_sys.lcl_l2.justification: perf list: Demand Data Cache Fills by Data Source, From Local L2 to the core. SMT siblings share the L1D, so a sibling's writes need no fill from L2; a nonzero count would indicate L1D evictions rather than inter-core transfer.

ls_locks.non_spec_lock.justification: perf list: Retired lock instructions, Non-speculative lock succeeded. The measured loop's only memory operation is a locked add; the event distinguishes the non-speculative completion path. Its microarchitectural meaning beyond that description is not claimed (no matching PPR was obtained).

l2_request_g1.rd_blk_x.justification: perf list: All L2 Cache Requests (Breakdown 1 - Common), Data cache stores. A locked add on a line this core does not hold writable must request it from L2; counts per increment measure how often that happened.

l2_cache_req_stat.ls_rd_blk_c.role: data requests that missed this core's L2
l2_cache_req_stat.ls_rd_blk_c.justification: perf list: Core to L2 cacheable request access status, Data cache request miss in L2 (all types). The generic cache-misses event on this kernel is event=0x64,umask=0x09 (L2 misses including instruction fetch), so it is an L2 count, not a last-level-cache count; this event isolates the data side.

ls_locks.spec_lock_hi_spec.justification: perf list: Retired lock instructions, High speculative cacheable lock speculation succeeded. Recorded beside the non-speculative count; together they show which documented completion paths the locked adds took.

hypotheses.claim: Line transfer: across cores, adjacent and shared slots make each increment wait for the 64-byte line to move between the two cores' private caches.
predictions: cross-core adjacent and shared cost many more cycles per increment than separate
their int_cache demand fills and L2 store requests per increment are far above separate's, which are near zero
hypotheses.falsified_if: cross-core adjacent shows no more fills or L2 store requests than separate, or no slowdown

hypotheses.claim: Lifecycle: the earlier campaign's difference came from thread creation, barrier and join, which its interval included.
predictions: if H2 holds, the in-thread steady-state difference between adjacent and separate is small beside the lifecycle time
hypotheses.falsified_if: the steady-state window difference is large while thread start time is similar across layouts

hypotheses.claim: Line transfer is the whole explanation, so removing it removes the cost: on SMT siblings, which share the L1D, adjacent slots should cost about what separate slots cost.
predictions: smt adjacent is close to smt separate
smt int_cache fills and L2 store requests are near zero
hypotheses.falsified_if: smt adjacent is still much slower than smt separate while its fills and L2 requests stay near zero; that would point to an in-core mechanism for same-line locked operations from two hardware threads

hypotheses.claim: Resource sharing or frequency: a running peer slows the measured thread whatever the layout, through shared execution resources (SMT) or a lower clock with two active cores.
predictions: smt separate is slower than smt solo
cross-core separate is close to cross-core solo
user cycles per ns differ between placements if the clock does
hypotheses.falsified_if: solo and separate cost the same on SMT siblings

hypotheses.claim: The line, not the slot, is the unit: true sharing (one slot) and false sharing (two slots in one line) cost about the same.
predictions: shared and adjacent differ little in cycles, fills and L2 requests per increment in each placement
hypotheses.falsified_if: shared and adjacent differ consistently; something beyond line ownership then matters

design_log: Smoke runs before this spec was frozen showed that a sleeping start barrier let one thread begin its window up to about 2 ms after the other; the start barrier now spins, every row records both windows, the peer's tail end and per-window context switches, and the analysis reports how much of the measured window the peer was active.

The same smoke runs showed nonzero int_cache fills only for cross-core adjacent/shared, zero change_to_x and lcl_l2 everywhere, and a large SMT adjacent cost with zero fills. Those observations chose the events above and made H3 a stated challenge; they are not evidence for any hypothesis. Only the gated runs are.
limits: Each thread counts only itself, user space only; kernel work (clock reads on this HPET host are system calls) is in elapsed time but not in counts.
Placement is per-thread affinity within the allowed set; other tasks may still run on the chosen CPUs or their siblings. Rows record load, per-CPU busy fractions and in-window context switches.
64 and 128 bytes are tested address interventions on a host reporting coherency_line_size 64, not a universal line size.
